item.title: Self review
item.description: Own your contributions, self-review your code, read it pretending you are someone else, you will find gaps, fix them before sending to review. Related to Code review pyramid, and Tips for Software Engineers.

item.title: Document incidents while they are happening
item.description: Shit happens, when they happen, it’s essential to document the steps and decisions made while solving it, so you can Use postmortems to learn from incidents ...

item.title: Use postmortems to learn from incidents
item.description: Ok, an incident happened! Production is down. Avoid the cover ass attitude and get moving to fix this. While you do that, Document incidents while they are happening, organise your team and move forward.

item.title: Avoid the cover ass attitude
item.description: When shit hits the fan, if it’s your fault, own it. If it’s someone else’s fault, own it. Do not focus on finding someone to blame; concentrate on sorting the problem out.

item.title: Communicate often
item.description: Work out loud, send updates about your progress, and communicate with your stakeholders. Let them know what is going on every day! My last action of the day is to communicate about my progress.

item.title: Write less code
item.description: Less is more; every single line of code is something you will have to maintain later. Do not fool yourself, you are liable to maintain any dependency you add to your code.

item.title: Choose dependencies wisely
item.description: We got used to installing a new package, using it and shipping it, pretending it’s production-ready. But there’s way more that comes with it. Before adding any dependencies, there are some things you must check: Is it still maintained? If not, what are the alternatives? When was the last time this package was updated? More than a year? How many issues are open? Check the issues, see if anything major is pending (you may save a couple of hours, just here) Are the pull requests being reviewed? Does it have tests? Quickly look around the code, try to make sense of it.

item.title: Don't leave dead code behind
item.description: Keep things tidy; if the code is not being used, remove it. Don’t get attached. You have source control to look for it if you happen to need it again. Believe me, you won’t need it.

item.title: AI coding warning
item.description: Enjoy the vibe, but remember, you are still responsible for your contributions. Do not lower your standards. AI tools can help you deliver more, but make sure to keep your standards ALWAYS review the bloody code properly and double-check dependencies.

item.title: All My HDDs Failed on UNRAID
item.description: This post documents the stress of having to replace all my HDDs on UNRAID after they began failing one after the other… all within a matter of days. They were 3.5 years old, all bought together, and used 24/7 — so, yeah, they retired in sync.
